strings.d1.s0.name: Colosseo
strings.d1.s0.tips: One ticket covers the Colosseum, Forum and Palatine Hill (about 18 EUR); book the 08:30 first slot online. The arena floor costs extra, there is no shade, so bring water.
strings.d1.s1.name: Foro Romano
strings.d1.s1.tips: Included in the same ticket; walk along the Via Sacra and see the Temple of Vesta.
strings.d1.s2.name: Palatino
strings.d1.s2.tips: Imperial palace ruins and views over the Forum; there is an orange grove.
strings.d1.s3.name: Trattoria Luzzi
strings.d1.s3.tips: A cheap, no-frills local trattoria next to the Colosseum; try the cacio e pepe. The queue moves fast.
strings.d1.s4.name: Piazza del Campidoglio
strings.d1.s4.tips: Michelangelo's square; the terrace behind it gives a free sunset view over the Forum.
strings.d1.b0.name: Li Rioni Pizzeria
strings.d1.b0.tips: Roman-style pizza near the Colosseum; open in the evening.
strings.d1.b1.name: Basilica di San Clemente
strings.d1.b1.tips: A three-level church built over a Roman temple; right next to the Colosseum.
strings.d2.s0.name: Musei Vaticani
strings.d2.s0.tips: Book the 08:00 first slot for the Sistine Chapel (25 EUR online, bookable 60 days ahead); expect the Raphael Rooms and long corridors.
strings.d2.s1.name: Basilica di San Pietro
strings.d2.s1.tips: Free to enter, but there is a security queue; the dome costs 10 EUR (551 steps), and the Pietà is by the entrance.
strings.d2.s2.name: Bonci Pizzarium
strings.d2.s2.tips: Gabriele Bonci's pizza by the slice; near Cipro metro station for the Vatican, eat standing up.
strings.d2.s3.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
strings.d2.s3.tips: Hadrian's mausoleum turned fortress; the terrace has views toward the Vatican.
strings.d2.s4.name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
strings.d2.s4.tips: Bernini's bridge lined with angels; photograph it before sunset.
strings.d2.b0.name: Pizzeria Da Remo Testaccio
strings.d2.b0.tips: Thin Roman pizza; evenings, in Testaccio.
strings.d2.b1.name: Giardini Vaticani
strings.d2.b1.tips: Guided tour of the Vatican Gardens; an alternative to the castle.
strings.d3.theme: Baroque Rome: Pantheon, Navona and Trevi
strings.d3.s0.name: Pantheon
strings.d3.s0.tips: See the oculus in the dome; entry is 5 EUR, the morning light is best, and Mass is held on Sundays.
strings.d3.s1.name: Piazza Navona
strings.d3.s1.tips: Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers; the cafes are pricey, so come for the photos.
strings.d3.s2.name: Campo de' Fiori
strings.d3.s2.tips: Morning market with cheese, spices and truffle products.
strings.d3.s3.name: Roscioli Salumeria
strings.d3.s3.tips: Carbonara and a deli counter display; booking is essential, and it is among the best in Rome.
strings.d3.s4.name: Trevi Fountain
strings.d3.s4.tips: Toss in a coin; it is empty at 07:00 or 23:00 and swamped by day (entry system in place since 2025).
strings.d3.b0.name: Armando al Pantheon
strings.d3.b0.tips: Roman cooking since 1961; next to the Pantheon, book ahead.
strings.d3.b1.name: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
strings.d3.b1.tips: A private palace collection with Caravaggio and Velázquez; a calm alternative to Trevi.
strings.d4.s0.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
strings.d4.s0.tips: One of Rome's oldest churches dedicated to Mary; golden mosaics, and quiet in the morning.
strings.d4.s1.name: Trastevere Streets
strings.d4.s1.tips: Cobblestones and ivy-covered walls; stroll Via della Lungaretta.
strings.d4.s2.name: Da Enzo al 29
strings.d4.s2.tips: A small Trastevere classic; amatriciana and artichokes. Join the queue when it opens at 12:00.
strings.d4.s3.name: Villa Farnesina
strings.d4.s3.tips: A Renaissance villa with Raphael frescoes; peaceful.
strings.d4.s4.name: Janiculum Terrace
strings.d4.s4.tips: Rome's best free view; the Garibaldi monument, and sunset.
strings.d4.b0.name: Trapizzino Trastevere
strings.d4.b0.tips: Stew stuffed in a pizza pocket; street food.
strings.d4.b1.name: Orto Botanico di Roma
strings.d4.b1.tips: A botanical garden in Trastevere; an alternative to the villa.
strings.d5.s0.name: Galleria Borghese
strings.d5.s0.tips: Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio; 2-hour slots, and booking weeks ahead is mandatory.
strings.d5.s1.name: Villa Borghese Gardens
strings.d5.s1.tips: Walk through the park; the Pincio terrace overlooks Piazza del Popolo.
strings.d5.s2.name: Spanish Steps
strings.d5.s2.tips: Sitting on the steps is banned; Via Condotti is nearby.
strings.d5.s3.name: Pastificio Guerra
strings.d5.s3.tips: Fresh pasta for 5 EUR just behind the Spanish Steps; there is a queue at 13:00.
strings.d5.s4.name: Ara Pacis
strings.d5.s4.tips: Augustus's altar of peace, housed in Richard Meier's glass pavilion; air-conditioned.
strings.d5.b0.name: Ginger Sapori e Salute
strings.d5.b0.tips: A light Italian lunch near the Spanish Steps.
strings.d5.b1.name: Piazza del Popolo
strings.d5.b1.tips: Twin churches and a Caravaggio (Santa Maria del Popolo, free).
strings.d6.s0.name: Villa d'Este
strings.d6.s0.tips: Renaissance fountain gardens in Tivoli; 500 jets, and open in winter too.
strings.d6.s1.name: Sibilla Ristorante Tivoli
strings.d6.s1.tips: A historic restaurant beside the Temple of Vesta; views over Tivoli.
strings.d6.s2.name: Villa Adriana
strings.d6.s2.tips: Hadrian's vast villa; the Canopus pool, and a 2-hour walk.
strings.d6.b0.name: Antica Trattoria del Falcone Tivoli
strings.d6.b1.name: Castelli Romani Frascati
strings.d6.b1.tips: A wine town in the hills outside Rome; an alternative to Ostia.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mercato Testaccio
strings.d7.s0.tips: Local market; try the beef stew sandwich at Mordi e Vai, and supplì (fried rice balls).
strings.d7.s1.name: Pyramid of Cestius and Non-Catholic Cemetery
strings.d7.s1.tips: A pyramid in Rome and the Keats-Shelley cemetery; look out for the cats.
strings.d7.s2.name: Aventine Orange Garden
strings.d7.s2.tips: Giardino degli Aranci and the Knights of Malta keyhole; a farewell view.
strings.d7.s3.name: Flavio al Velavevodetto
strings.d7.s3.tips: A trattoria carved into Monte Testaccio; carbonara and coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew).
strings.d7.s4.name: Roma Termini
strings.d7.s4.tips: The Leonardo Express reaches Fiumicino in 32 minutes; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Trapizzino Testaccio
strings.d7.b0.tips: Stew stuffed in a pizza pocket; a quick farewell bite.
strings.d7.b1.name: Baths of Caracalla
strings.d7.b1.tips: Ruins of a huge Roman bathhouse; an alternative to the pyramid.
strings.note0: Rome is walkable; metro lines A and B are limited, and bus 64 goes to the Vatican. The Leonardo Express to Fiumicino costs 14 EUR. The Roma Pass (48/72 hours) covers museums and transport.
strings.note1: Timed online tickets are ESSENTIAL for the Colosseum, Vatican Museums and Borghese; book Borghese weeks ahead and the Vatican 60 days ahead.
strings.note2: Winter is 8-14°C and rainy, but without the crowds; the Colosseum and Vatican are calm, Piazza Navona has its Christmas market, and January brings sales.
strings.note3: Rome's four pastas: carbonara, cacio e pepe, amatriciana, gricia; the coperto (cover charge) is 2-3 EUR, and tipping means rounding up.
strings.note4: Cover shoulders and knees in churches (the Vatican is strict); the fountains (nasoni) give drinkable water, so refill your bottle.
strings.note5: Watch for pickpockets on bus 64 and at Termini; say 'no grazie' to bracelet sellers at Trevi and the Spanish Steps.
